mcat_description.short: A PVC Toilet is a prefabricated, readymade sanitation cabin constructed from PVC panels, sold as a complete portable unit with toilet fittings, water tank, and door — available in Indian squat or Western commode styles.
mcat_description.long: PVC Toilets are factory-manufactured portable sanitation structures built from PVC (polyvinyl chloride) panels for walls, roof, and floor, forming a self-contained cabin unit that can be transported and installed without civil construction work. They are sold as complete readymade units pre-fitted with a toilet pan (Indian squat or Western WC), overhead water tank, wash basin, exhaust fan, and door — designed for plug-and-use deployment at construction sites, public events, rural sanitation programmes, and institutional campuses. The PVC material provides corrosion resistance, low maintenance, and weather resistance, making these units suitable for outdoor and semi-permanent use across India's varied climates. Units are available as single-compartment standalone cabins or as multi-compartment toilet blocks, with customisation options for size, colour, and fittings.

market_context: PVC Toilets in the Indian B2B market refer to prefabricated portable sanitation cabins constructed from PVC panels, sold as complete readymade units. The market offers two primary toilet style variants — Indian squat (squatting pan) and Western commode — with Indian style being the dominant form for construction site and rural sanitation applications. Key material competitors in the portable toilet cabin segment include FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), HDPE, MS (mild steel), and PUF sandwich panel constructions; PVC is positioned as the most economical and lightweight option. Units are typically available in standard sizes ranging from approximately 3×3×7 ft to 4×4×8.6 ft for single-compartment cabins, with multi-compartment blocks available up to 10 units. Common included fittings are overhead water tank (typically 100–200 litres), wash basin, exhaust fan, and door with latch. The Swachh Bharat Mission and government rural sanitation programmes are significant demand drivers for bulk procurement. Buyers include construction contractors, government/municipal bodies, event managers, NGOs, and industrial facility managers. No specific BIS IS standard governs PVC portable toilet cabins (unconfirmed — no standard number found in available sources); however, manufacturers reference IS-grade materials for structural components. Recognised trade names include Sintex Portolet and Sintex Sugam Toilet (PUF-based), Modcon, and JRMS. The term 'plastic toilet' is used interchangeably with 'PVC toilet' in buyer vocabulary.
